info.name: Digilux — Google Home Cloud-to-Cloud
info.description:
API collection for the Google Home Cloud-to-Cloud account linking integration.

Flutter-facing flow (run in order):
  1. POST   /api/v1/voice/google-home/account-linking/deep-link/start  → get state + deep link
  2. (User opens Google Home app or web OAuth, completes login)
  3. GET    /api/v1/voice/google-home/account-linking                  → poll until linked=true
  4. POST   /api/v1/voice/google-home/account-linking/deep-link/complete → finalise session
  5. DELETE /api/v1/voice/google-home/account-linking                  → unlink

Google-facing endpoints (called automatically by Google — for manual QA only):
  - POST /google-home/oauth/authorize  (App Flip path)
  - POST /google-home/oauth/token      (authorization_code + refresh_token)
  - POST /google-home/fulfillment      (SYNC / QUERY / EXECUTE / DISCONNECT)

Variables required:
  - base_url          : API Gateway base URL (e.g. https://iot.digilux.co.in/smarthome)
  - cognito_token     : Cognito ACCESS token from app login
  - gh_state          : Auto-populated from the start response
  - gh_client_id      : Google OAuth client ID (from env.digilux.qa.json)
  - gh_client_secret  : Google OAuth client secret (from Secrets Manager)
  - gh_auth_code      : Auth code issued by authorize endpoint (for token endpoint tests)
  - gh_access_token   : Auto-populated from token endpoint response
  - gh_refresh_token  : Auto-populated from token endpoint response

item.name: Flutter Flow
item.description: Endpoints called by the Flutter app. Run in this order: Start → (Google OAuth) → Poll Status → Complete → (later) Unlink.

exec: console.log('NEXT: Open homeAppDeepLink on a real device, or run the App Flip request manually.');
console.log('Then poll Step 2 (Status) until linked=true, then run Step 3 (Complete).');

request.description:
Creates a `PENDING` session in `google_home_link_sessions` DynamoDB (TTL 1800s).

Returns:
- `state` — CSRF token, saved to `gh_state` variable
- `agentId` — Google Home agent ID (`digilux-ai-pro`)
- `homeAppDeepLink` — URL to open the Google Home app at the account linking screen
- `webFallbackUrl` — OAuth web URL if GH app is not installed

**No request body required.**

exec: console.log('Run Step 3 — Complete to finalise the Flutter session.');
console.log('Not linked yet. Keep polling or complete the OAuth flow in Google Home.');

request.description:
Reads `google_home_tokens` DynamoDB for the current user.

**No request body required.**

Flutter polls this every 2 seconds for up to 10 minutes after opening the GH deep link.
Returns `linked: true` as soon as Google has completed the token exchange (i.e. `google_home_oauth_token` has run and stored the tokens).

exec: console.warn('gh_state is empty — run Step 1 first.');
console.log('Session complete. Google Home is linked.');

request.description:
Updates the session in `google_home_link_sessions` from `PENDING` to `LINKED`.
Called by Flutter after the user returns from the Google Home OAuth flow.

Verifies the session state belongs to the authenticated user and hasn't expired.
Returns `{ "linked": true }` on success.

exec: console.log('Note: GH app reflects this immediately only if GOOGLE_SA_KEY_SECRET_ARN is configured.');
console.log('Otherwise GH app updates within ~1 hour when the access token expires.');

request.description:
Unlinks the authenticated user's Google Home account.

**No request body required.**

**What the backend does (in order):**
1. Looks up the user's token record in `google_home_tokens` DynamoDB
2. **Best-effort:** calls Google Home Graph API `deleteAgentUser` (requires `GOOGLE_SA_KEY_SECRET_ARN`) — makes GH app reflect the unlinked state immediately
3. Deletes the token record from `google_home_tokens` DynamoDB
4. Returns `{ "linked": false }`

**Idempotent** — returns 200 even if user was already unlinked.

**If `GOOGLE_SA_KEY_SECRET_ARN` is not set:** GH app still shows linked for up to ~1 hour until the access token we issued to Google expires and Google attempts a refresh (which will fail with `invalid_grant`, causing GH to mark the account as disconnected).

item.description: Called automatically by the Google Home app and Google's servers. Use these for manual QA and debugging — not part of the normal Flutter flow.

console.log('Run Token Exchange — Authorization Code to get access + refresh tokens.');

header.description: Cognito access token — simulates the App Flip path where GoogleHomeAppFlipActivity passes the user's token

request.description:
App Flip path — simulates `GoogleHomeAppFlipActivity` sending the user's Cognito access token.

The lambda detects the `Authorization: Bearer` header and skips the login form.
It validates the token via Cognito `GetUser`, issues an auth code into `google_home_auth_codes` DynamoDB (TTL 900s), and returns:
```json
{"code": "<auth_code>", "state": ""}
```

The auth code is auto-saved to `gh_auth_code` for the Token Exchange request.

exec: console.warn('gh_auth_code is empty. Run Authorize — App Flip first to get a code.');
console.log('Run Poll Status or Fulfillment SYNC to verify the account is linked.');

urlencoded.description: Auth code from the authorize endpoint (single-use, 900s TTL)
Google OAuth client secret from Secrets Manager
Must match the redirect_uri used in the authorize step

request.description:
Called by Google's servers to exchange the auth code for tokens. Simulated here for QA.

**What the backend does:**
1. Validates `client_id` + `client_secret` against Secrets Manager
2. Looks up and deletes the auth code from `google_home_auth_codes` (single-use)
3. Issues opaque `access_token` + `refresh_token` (random strings, NOT Google tokens)
4. Stores both in `google_home_tokens` DynamoDB (this is the event that makes `linked=true`)

The `access_token` and `refresh_token` are saved to collection variables for use in fulfillment requests.

exec: console.warn('gh_refresh_token is empty. Run Token Exchange first.');
console.log('Access token refreshed. New prefix:', res.access_token.substring(0, 8) + '...');

urlencoded.description: Refresh token from the initial token exchange

request.description:
Issues a new access token without requiring re-authentication.

The refresh token stays the same. Only the access token and its expiry are updated in DynamoDB.

If the refresh token is not found (e.g. user already unlinked), returns `invalid_grant`.

item.name: Fulfillment (Google-facing)
item.description: Called by Google's servers for voice commands. Use `gh_access_token` (opaque token we issued) as the Bearer token — NOT a Cognito token.

header.description: Opaque access token issued by our token endpoint — NOT a Cognito token

request.description:
Triggered by Google when the user says "Hey Google, sync my devices" or after account linking.

The lambda resolves the `gh_access_token` to a `userId` via the `accessToken-index` GSI, then reads `digilux_user_device_mapping` DynamoDB to return the user's sites as Google Home scene devices.

header.description: Opaque access token issued by our token endpoint

request.description:
Triggered when the user asks "Hey Google, is [device] on?".

**NOTE:** Currently returns a placeholder `{ "online": true }` for all devices. Device state from the Digilux control API is not yet integrated.

header.description: Opaque access token issued by our token endpoint

request.description:
Sent by Google when the user unlinks from within the Google Home app.

The lambda deletes the user's token record from `google_home_tokens` DynamoDB and returns an empty payload. Google expects HTTP 200 with `{}` payload.

This is the Google-initiated unlink path. The Digilux-app-initiated unlink uses the `DELETE /api/v1/voice/google-home/account-linking` endpoint instead, which also calls the Home Graph `deleteAgentUser` API.

request.description: Uses a token that no longer exists in google_home_tokens. Expect 401. This is what Google will see after a user unlinks — Google will then initiate a token refresh, which will also fail (invalid_grant), causing GH to mark the account as disconnected.
